title: DARPA's FAR exception and canceled stealth program

plain: John Blitch, a scientist who worked at DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, says that in the late 1990s he ran a $130 million portfolio there under an exception to the government's normal purchasing rules, half of it robots and half a stealth programme that was canceled "a month after it began, again for no reason." Blitch tells Michels this from his own experience and says it fits what General Arthur Trudeau, the Army's research chief in the 1950s and 60s, told Philip J. Corso, an officer under him, to do with recovered technology, which if true would mean hidden programmes were being quietly started and shut down.
